chapter: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
title: Ben Webster's humor and storytelling
summary: Leeman adds that Ben Webster was a champion storyteller who built tales slowly to a climax, much as he built his solos.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: After taping days, and nights when I try to relax, I think of some of the things that we covered, and every once

in awhile, I jot something down, and I'll say, "Gee, I forgot to mention this or that". I wanted to say about Ben Webster. I didn't bring it up that -- you see, nobody mentioned Ben Webster's great sense of humor. If you talked to anybody that knew him, that's one of the first things they'll mention, along with his playing, and the fact that he was a champion among storytellers.

A great many true humorous incidents of musicians and a great many fabricated incidents were a part of his storytelling. He would taken an extraordinary amount of time building a tale, never losing its interest along the way, to an extraordinary climax and a burst of hilarious emotional outlets. And in passing along this information, which people should know, I sometimes think his playing was a great deal patterned in that vein -- possibly he was unaware of it.
